## GeoML

## Network

Turning a line layer into a graph, and seeing exactly how much a snap
tolerance changes how many pieces the network actually has — runnable
Python and R code side by side, plus a force-directed diagram of the
graph itself.

**[Network from Lines](posts/network-from-lines.qmd)**

## GeoStatistics

Predicting a continuous surface from sparse point samples, and filling
the gaps in a surface you already have — fitting a variogram model to
how similar nearby points really are, instead of just averaging
distance-weighted neighbors. Runs on R only; Python is shown as
reference, with the reason explained plainly.

**[Kriging Interpolator](posts/kriging-soil-sampling.qmd)** →
**[Filling Raster Gaps with Cokriging](posts/cokriging-raster-gap-filling.qmd)**
